stem:
Farai Chitepo owns Chitepo General Dealer in Masvingo. He does not keep a ledger. The information below is taken from his bank statements, invoices and till rolls for the year ended 31 December 2025.

| Equipment: cost | 16,400 |  |
| Equipment: accumulated depreciation | 4,100 |  |
| Stock | 8,615 | 9,380 |
| Debtors | 3,245 | 3,880 |
| Provision for doubtful debts | 160 | to be calculated |
| Creditors | 4,630 | 4,255 |
| Wages owing | 270 | 335 |
| Rent prepaid | 405 | 405 |
| Delivery expenses owing |  | 305 |
| Bank | 2,185 | 3,015 |

| Transactions during the year | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Customers paid | 47,915 |
| Discount allowed | 545 |
| Returns inwards | 845 |
| Bad debts written off | 315 |
| Cash sales (all banked) | 12,860 |
| Suppliers paid | 31,420 |

| Wages paid | 11,840 |
| Rent paid | 4,860 |
| Delivery expenses paid | 2,180 |
| General expenses paid | 2,935 |
| Equipment bought and paid from the bank | 2,700 |

Equipment is depreciated at 10% of the cost of equipment held at the year end. The provision for doubtful debts is to be 5% of debtors at the year end. All other withdrawals from the bank were drawings. The statements are for internal use.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate Farai's capital at 1 January 2025 (include the rent prepaid and the wages and electricity owing as given).
parts.explanation: Assets: equipment 12,300, stock 8,615, debtors less provision 3,085, prepaid rent 405, bank 2,185 = 26,590. Liabilities: creditors 4,630 and wages owing 270 = 4,900. Capital = 21,690.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Assets: equipment 12,300, stock 8,615, debtors less provision 3,085, prepaid rent 405, bank 2,185 = 26,590. Liabilities: creditors 4,630 and wages owing 270 = 4,900. Capital = 21,690.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the credit sales for the year.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the credit purchases for the year.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate Farai's drawings for the year (remember the equipment bought).
parts.explanation: Bank receipts 62,960 less payments 55,935 less closing bank 3,015 = 4,010.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Bank receipts 62,960 less payments 55,935 less closing bank 3,015 = 4,010.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the total charge to the income statement for bad debts and the change in the provision for doubtful debts.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit for the year.
parts.explanation: Sales 63,115 less returns 845 = 62,270; cost of sales 30,745; gross profit 31,525; add discount received 465; expenses 24,989; profit 7,001.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Sales 63,115 less returns 845 = 62,270; cost of sales 30,745; gross profit 31,525; add discount received 465; expenses 24,989; profit 7,001.

parts.stem: Prepare the income statement for the year ended 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: State two limitations of using incomplete records.

points.description: Balancing figures such as drawings absorb unrecorded items, so errors are not detected
No detailed records of sales and expenses, so profit and control are less reliable

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Errors are not detected because drawings and sales are balancing figures, and the lack of detailed records makes it hard to control the business and verify the profit.

explanation: This item tests the reconstruction of figures from incomplete records, the profit for the year and the income statement.
hints: Write a total account for debtors and for creditors.
Expense for the year = cash paid adjusted for accruals and prepayments.

stem:
Takura, Nyasha and Rudo are in partnership as hardware merchants in Gweru. The partnership agreement provides for: a salary of US\$5,000 a year for Nyasha; interest on capital at 5% a year; interest charged on drawings at 4% of the drawings for the year; and the residual profit to be shared in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1 (Takura : Nyasha : Rudo).

The capital accounts are fixed: Takura US\$36,000, Nyasha US\$28,000, Rudo US\$16,000. Drawings for the year ended 31 December 2025 were Takura US\$7,850, Nyasha US\$8,400 and Rudo US\$5,250. Current account balances at 1 January 2025 were Takura US\$1,630 credit, Nyasha US\$910 debit and Rudo US\$2,215 credit. The net profit for the year was US\$54,004.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the total interest on capital for the year.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the total interest charged on drawings.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the residual profit to be shared.
parts.explanation: 54,004 + interest on drawings 860 - salary 5,000 - interest on capital 4,000 = 45,864.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 54,004 + interest on drawings 860 - salary 5,000 - interest on capital 4,000 = 45,864.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the total profit appropriated to Nyasha (salary, interest on capital and share of residual, less interest on drawings).
parts.explanation: Salary 5,000 + interest 1,400 + share 15,288 - interest on drawings 336 = 21,352.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Salary 5,000 + interest 1,400 + share 15,288 - interest on drawings 336 = 21,352.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the balance on Rudo's current account at 31 December 2025 (credit).

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Prepare the profit and loss appropriation account for the year ended 31 December 2025.

points.description: Heading and net profit with interest on drawings added
Interest on capital deducted for each partner

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Explain why partners may agree to charge interest on drawings.

points.description: It discourages partners from withdrawing money early
Partners who draw more than others are charged for the use of the firm's funds
It treats the partners fairly because the firm loses the use of money withdrawn

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Interest on drawings discourages early withdrawals. A partner who draws more uses more of the firm's funds, so the charge is fair to the others.

explanation: This item tests the appropriation account and current accounts of a three-partner firm.
hints: Add interest on drawings to the profit before sharing.
Fixed capital: all entries go through the current accounts.
